selection.coreTest: A user who selected only this category would intentionally open the item because the category-specific information, consequence, or use case is central.
selection.directness: A category may be core through the event subject, action, consequence, or direct use case. A source label, format, actor name, incidental noun, or remote second-order effect is not enough.
promptRules: Accept every category that independently passes the core-user-value test.
Multiple categories are correct when each is a direct reason that a user of that category would open the item.
A secondary subject never grants admission.
A source section, publisher identity, content format, actor name, or incidental noun never grants admission by itself.
The same item is displayed once even when it is admitted to several selected categories.
If no category is independently core, withhold the item instead of forcing a label.

categories.core: General public-affairs, society, or world events whose main user value is broad current-awareness and is not fully represented by a more precise category.
categories.exclude: Do not admit news merely because the item is reporting, comes from a news outlet, or mentions a public event already fully owned by a precise domain category.

categories.core: Computing, software, hardware, AI, security, digital products, or technology-industry actions that directly change capabilities, supply, access, products, or the technology ecosystem.
categories.exclude: Do not admit tech when a technology name or company is only incidental and the event has no direct consequence for technology users or the technology ecosystem.

categories.core: Vehicles, mobility, driving, ownership, vehicle technology, or a policy or business action with a direct consequence for vehicles, drivers, or the automotive market.
categories.exclude: Do not admit auto when a vehicle maker or car is merely named in an unrelated corporate, celebrity, or general event.

categories.core: Scientific research, discovery, evidence, methods, institutions, or policy whose scientific content or consequence is central.
categories.exclude: Do not admit science for a technology product, health claim, or marketing statement that contains no meaningful scientific finding, evidence, or process.

categories.core: Markets, macroeconomics, finance, investment, earnings, corporate strategy, trade, labor, monetary policy, or a direct economic consequence.
categories.exclude: Do not admit business merely because a company, price, sponsor, or owner is named when the event itself has no material economic or corporate consequence.

categories.core: Games, gameplay, releases, platforms, game communities, esports, or gaming-specific hardware, configuration, purchasing, or performance use.
categories.exclude: Do not admit gaming for general computing or entertainment content that only mentions a game without direct value to a gaming user.

categories.core: Competitions, athletes, teams, sports performance, leagues, transfers, results, or operations that directly affect the sport or its audience.
categories.exclude: Do not admit sports for an unrelated action by a team owner, sponsor, or parent company that has no direct sports consequence.

categories.core: Film, television, music, celebrities, publishing, entertainment, cultural events, or media works whose cultural or entertainment value is central.
categories.exclude: Do not admit culture merely because a famous person, title, or entertainment company appears in an otherwise unrelated event.

categories.core: Health, food, home, travel, family, pets, fitness, practical hobbies, daily living, or actionable personal advice.
categories.exclude: Do not admit life for a generic human-interest angle when a more precise category contains the actual reason to open the item.

categories.core: Humor, memes, comedy, amusing stories, or everyday posts where entertainment or shared amusement is itself the main value.
categories.exclude: Do not admit humor merely because a serious item was posted on a humor board or uses an amusing phrase.

categories.core: Elections, parties, legislation, governance, public policy, political power, accountability, or a government action whose political or policy consequence is central.
categories.exclude: Do not admit politics for a politician's incidental comment or for an independent central-bank monetary operation unless political conflict or accountability is itself central.

categories.core: Housing, property, land, rent, mortgages, development, construction markets, or policy with a direct property or housing consequence.
categories.exclude: Do not admit realestate for a general interest-rate, company, or household story without a direct property, housing, or development consequence.

categories.core: Clothing, footwear, style, fashion products, designers, trends, retail, or fashion-industry actions with direct value to fashion users.
categories.exclude: Do not admit fashion merely because a person wears an item or a fashion brand is named in an unrelated culture or business event.

categories.core: Art, design, architecture, exhibitions, creative works, artists, or creative practice whose artistic or design value is central.
categories.exclude: Do not admit art when design is only a marketing adjective or an artwork or artist is incidental to another event.

productDecisions.summary: Gaming-specific PC build, configuration, purchase, or performance advice is directly useful to both technology and gaming users.
